title: Press the slot latch and lift the graphics card out
instruction: Press and hold the orange latch with the right hand, then lift the graphics card straight up with the left hand and put it in the tray on the left.
context: E-waste recyclers and IT asset disposal technicians pull graphics cards from thousands of dead boards for resale or precious-metal recovery. The PCIe slot's retention latch has to be pressed first: a card pulled against the latch breaks it, and a card pulled at an angle jams in the slot. One hand holds the latch down while the other lifts.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Mat: a 34 x 30 cm dark blue-grey rubber anti-static mat (34 cm along y), 3 mm thick, fixed, centred at (0.29, -0.04). Mainboard: a 30 x 24 cm green glass-epoxy board (30 cm along y), 2 mm thick, lying flat on the mat, fixed, centred at (0.29, -0.04), with its usual parts (processor socket, memory slots with black clips, two empty slots, small heatsinks), none taller than 1.2 cm and at least 1.5 cm from the card and the latch (the groove cover is flush). Slot: a black PCIe x16 slot along y, from y = -0.11 to y = -0.02 at x = 0.28, between two black plastic rails 9 cm long, 4 mm wide and 12 mm tall, 2.4 cm apart inside (2 mm of play each side of the card). Graphics card: an 18 x 11 cm dual-fan card, 2 cm thick with its black cooler and backplate, steel bracket at its far end, 350 g, standing upright in the slot along y with its bottom edge on the board, from y = -0.11 to y = 0.07, so it overhangs the slot's left end by 9 cm, bracket on the left, fans facing the robot. It is locked in the slot by the latch and comes out straight up only, and the rails are pried if it tilts 5 degrees or more while its bottom is between them. Latch: an orange plastic button 2 x 1.2 cm standing 1.2 cm out of a black housing (2.6 x 1.8 cm, 8 mm tall) on the board, in line with the slot at (0.28, -0.175), 2 cm along y, 5.5 cm right of the card's right end, sprung (500 N/m, 0 N at rest, 2 N at full travel), 4 mm of travel. Locking linkage, inside the board and the card's end cap and not drawn: the card's near end carries a steel end plate with a 9 mm tall hole, its lower edge 1.5 mm above the card's bottom edge. A spring-loaded steel pin 3 mm across, axis 8 mm above the board, passes through the hole 5 mm above its lower edge, so a seated card can rise 5 mm before the edge meets the pin. The pin is on a 5 cm steel push rod in a covered groove along the slot's axis, flush with the board, and the rod's other end has a 45 degree wedge under the button. Pressing the button 3 mm slides the rod 3 mm and pulls the pin 3 mm out of the hole (2.5 mm was in it): the card is free while the button is down. Let go, and the spring pushes the pin back into the hole if the card is raised less than 5 mm. If the card is already raised 5 mm or more, the pin meets the plate's face and the card stays free. The pin holds 60 N: pulled harder, or raised 5 mm or more with the button up and the pin in the hole, it is overloaded and the latch is broken. Tray: a 25 x 15 cm black plastic tray (25 cm along x), 1 cm walls 3 cm high, with a 1 cm grey foam floor, fixed on the robot's left at (0.24, 0.26). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Positions are centres, read at every control step. The button counts as pressed while it is 3 mm or more down: nothing about an earlier press is remembered. The latch is broken, and the trial scores 0 from then on (even if the card is then put in the tray), if the card is 5 mm or more above its start, or 3 cm or more sideways, while the button is up and the pin was in the hole at the step before (so pulling without pressing, or pressing and letting go before pulling, breaks it), or if the card tilts 5 degrees or more from upright while its bottom is between the rails (slot pried). 0 if the card falls off the table (centre more than 2 cm below the top). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): no gripper on the card (TCP within 3 cm of the card with the pads 4 mm or less wider than its 2 cm thickness), the card's centre within 9 cm along x and 5 cm along y of the tray's centre, its four lowest corners within 3 mm of the foam floor (lying on a face, not held up or leaning on a wall), and still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). 0.5: card out of the slot (centre 1.2 cm or more above its start, or 3 cm or more sideways) but not meeting 1.0: held in the air, held in or above the tray, or set down out of the tray. 0.25: card raised 5 mm or more but still between the rails. 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: If the lock was broken, fit a fresh pin and rod (it must hold 60 N again), and check that the rails are straight. Seat the card in the slot with its near end at x = 0.26 so the pin is in the hole, with the button up.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Every part collides as a box, the card is one 18 x 2 x 11 cm box and meshes are drawn only. The pin, rod and wedge are not bodies: the lock is a fixed joint that breaks at 60 N, switched off while the button is 3 mm down and on again when the button is up and the card is seated (1 mm), read every step. The button is a sprung prismatic joint. Pad grip 50 N each. Masses are typical.
scores: Demo: 1.0 (success at step 215). Dream-1 was not run on this version.
